dedupe_keys.name: state emergency food stockpiling in germany switzerland and finland comparative analysis kit 2024

description: This case study compares how Germany, Switzerland and Finland keep state emergency stocks of food, three countries known for active crisis preparedness. Researchers at the Institute for Industrial Production of the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, funded by the German food ministry through its agriculture and food agency, analysed each country's supply situation, stockpiling strategy and its history, storage system, costs and financing, and how stocks were used in selected crises. The evidence comes from a comparative content analysis, a literature review and interviews with experts in each country. The authors find marked differences between the national approaches and set out their advantages and disadvantages for policy makers and practitioners. The 57-page working paper, written in German, is free to download from KITopen under the KITopen licence. Coverage is the national systems of Germany, Switzerland and Finland as of 2024. Caveats: a qualitative policy comparison with no quantitative dataset; the facts here come from the abstract and contents pages. Simulation uses: parameters and rules for stockpile release in food supply disruption models and for scenario exercises. Related records: the USDA cold storage statistics (data-usda-nass-cold-storage) give stock quantities of a different, commercial kind.
